clusters.title: His space before a slash ('L6x6x1 /2', 'L6 x6 x1 /2') cuts the thickness to '1', and a REAL other angle (L6X6X1, L8X6X1, L8X8X1) is used silently, in look-ups AND calculations + 'Standard hole' / 'per Table J3.3' / 'nominal diameter of a standard hole' is answered with her NET-AREA hole (bolt + 1/8) + U from Table D3.1: '4 lines' is taken as 4 bolts per line (an invented second item printed clean), and 'through its web and flanges' is read as web only (case 7 instead of case 1)
clusters.root_cause:
[shape-name-split-fraction] reader.js findShapes: FR (l.150) accepts 'd d/d', 'd/d', '.d' and 'd', but not 'd /d' or 'd/ d'. So the L regex (l.166; the same applies to 2L l.164, HSS l.168 and plates) ends the name at '1', and the leftover ' /2' is masked and never questioned. The shape exists, so nothing stops. I confirmed it reaches calculations on the branch: 'L6x6x1 /2 tension member welded find phi pn' prints phi Pn = 495 kips from L6X6X1 (Ag 11). HSS6x6x1 /2 and L4x4x1 /2 are refused only because those names do not exist. expand.js FRQ (l.62) has the same gap. His own typing model lists '3 /4' as normal.
[standard-hole] The frozen finder routes these to lookup_hole. reader.js FILL.lookup_hole (l.2555) reads only the bolt, and the engine's ANSWER is always 'Hole size for net area: bolt + 1/8'. The J3.3 standard hole appears only in the engine's step 2 text. No reader or pipeline guard reads 'standard' / 'J3.3' / 'nominal hole'. Only expand.js parseHole (l.357) declines them, and only for lists. The corpus has the same clean wrong line on q15, h02 and the whole BL-031 family (8 variants, 'According to Table J3.3 ... nominal diameter of a standard hole for a 3/4 in. bolt' -> 0.875 where 13/16 is right). Her rules.js ('standard = bolt + 1/16') and J3.3 (bolt + 1/8 from 1 in up) also disagree for 1 in bolts.
[shear-lag-U-reading] (a) expand.js parseU (l.397-407): COUNT_RE (l.393) takes any bare digit, and 'lines' is a filler in FILL_U (l.395). So in '3 bolts per line, 4 lines' the '4' becomes a second bolts-per-line count, and itemsOf writes part (b) 'with 4 bolts per line'. Part (a) refuses correctly, but part (b) prints U = 0.70 / 0.85 clean (look-52/53). '4 bolts per line, 2 lines' gives the same false split (b refused). (b) reader.js findHoles location regex (l.1192) captures only the FIRST element after 'through its' ('connected through its web'), so 'and flanges' sets no locFlange. tensionCommon (l.1712) then sets conn = 'web' (case 7, 0.70). The engine's 'all' (case 1, U = 1.0, checked) is never chosen (look-54).
clusters.fix_plan:
[shape-name-split-fraction] reader.js (and expand.js FRQ for lists). (1) FR: add the alternatives '\\d+\\s+\\/\\s*\\d+|\\d+\\s*\\/\\s+\\d+' (a space on either side of the slash) after the mixed-number alternative, so 'x1 /2' reads 1/2. Edit with the Edit tool (backslashes). compactDim / legName must remove the inner spaces of the fraction before the name is built ('1 /2' -> '1/2'). (2) Safety net in findShapes: a shape match whose next characters are \\s*\\/\\s*\\d (a fraction left over) is not read. The part then STOPs/ASKs for the shape, instead of using a shorter real name. ANSWER: look-46 L6X6X1/2 A = 5.77, look-47 L8X6X1/2 A = 6.80, look-48 5.77, and the tension example uses Ag 5.77. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'L5x3-1/2x1/2' / 'L5 x 3 1/2 x 1/2' legs, 'L4x4x1/2, 3/4 in bolts' (a comma, not a slash), 'PL 1/2 x 10', '1 1/2' mixed numbers, 'W10/W12' families, the bolt '3 /4 in' reading. Run regress.sh and look at every shape-name change.
[standard-hole] reader.js FILL.lookup_hole only (smallest safe). When the words ask the STANDARD hole itself: /\\bstandard\\s+hole|\\btable\\s+j\\s?3\\.?3\\b|\\bnominal\\s+(?:hole|diameter\\s+of\\s+(?:a|the)\\s+(?:standard\\s+)?hole)|\\bover-?sized?\\s+hole|\\bslot/i, with no 'net area|deduct|for computing|to subtract' in the same sentence. Then B.ask('std_hole', one sentence with no number, [], null, 'stop'): 'Your question asks the standard hole of the Specification's hole table; this page gives only the hole width her net-area rule deducts. NOT answered here.' No digits ('J3.3' has digits, so do not quote it). Optional later, only after the stop is in: a pipeline ANSWER TO line from the engine's step text 'Table J3.3 lists the standard hole itself as X in' (13/16, 15/16, 1-1/8), with the net-area line demoted to ALSO FOUND. Unambiguous per J3.3, but it needs a pipeline hunk. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'hole diameter for a 3/4in bolt' / 'hole size for net area' (bolt + 1/8, her rule: q14, a16, x01, x02, BL-030 family, BL-032, BL-043), 'standard holes' inside tension questions (k24 is tension_net_area, not lookup_hole), A2-words-39.
[shear-lag-U-reading] (1) expand.js COUNT_RE: add a negative lookahead so a number followed by \\s+(?:gage\\s+)?(?:lines?|rows?) is not a count. The digit then stays in the residue, parseU returns null, and the single reader takes the question whole: look-52/53 STOP (3 per line in the web / 2 per line in the flanges is not case 7), and '4 bolts per line, 2 lines' ANSWERs 0.70 once. (2) reader.js findHoles, after the location loop: /(?:through|in|to|at)\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+|both\\s+)?(?:web\\s+and\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+|both\\s+)?flanges?|flanges?\\s+and\\s+(?:its\\s+|the\\s+)?web)\\b|\\ball\\s+(?:its\\s+)?(?:elements|parts)\\b/ sets both H.locWeb and H.locFlange. The existing 'hasF && hasW' branch then sets conn 'all', so ANSWER U = 1.0 (case 1, every element connected, her case 1). 'no holes/bolts in the web' must still win (noWeb), and so must lane L1's negation scoping. MUST NOT CHANGE: 'U for 3 and 4 bolts per line' lists, 'connected through the flanges only' / 'web only', case 7/8 values (0.90/0.85/0.70/0.80/0.60), her May 2024 Q8 'four lines ... through its flanges'.

clusters.title: A steel grade typed with a product or shape (A36 angle, A572 Gr 50 plate, A500 Gr B HSS, 'gr 50', A53 pipe) is ignored: the product's slide default or the form's Fy = 50 is printed + The steel or bolt of something else becomes the member's: A36 gusset/end plates, 'not a36', the cover's 'A36 for plates', an inline default bolt; a short defaults line is read as the question's own words, and a long one drops its U
clusters.root_cause:
[named-steel-grade] Four places. (a) reader.js FILL.lookup_material (l.2551-2554) fills 'what' from the shape (high) or a product word (medium) and never reads a typed grade. pipeline.js markGrade (l.2949-2953) reads a grade only when that box is EMPTY, so the product or shape default wins (look-07..12). The corpus shows the same misses: m08, g06, g07, g08, g10, g11, g09. (b) expand.js chunksOf (l.233-243) cuts at ',' and parseMat (l.297-327) makes 'plate, A572 Gr. 50' / 'L4x4x1/2 ,A36' into TWO items: (a) the product default, clean, and (b) the grade (look-13/14). (c) FILL.lookup_critical_stress (l.2022-2026) calls fillFy (l.1476), which reads only a typed Fy or a GRADES row (l.1233). GRADES has no A53 / A500 row, product words (pipe, plate, HSS) are never consulted, and 'grade B' is not read. So the form's Fy 50 is used silently (look-15..18). (d) findGrade (l.1255) takes the FIRST 'Fy = n ksi'. A second, different Fy never stops (look-19). 'gr 50' with no A-number is read by nothing (look-12). The engine refuses 'A500 Grade B' (not on her slide), so the existing markGrade path cannot answer look-11 either.
[grade-and-cover-binding] reader.js findGrade (1252-1270) loops GRADES with A36 FIRST and keeps the first grade found anywhere (pickMatch falls back to any match). So the steel of gusset, end or base plates, 'not a36', 'instead of a36' and the cover's 'A36 for plates' all become the member's steel, and two grades are never treated as a conflict. Cover and defaults: splitPreamble (484) makes a cover line preamble only when it is > 80 characters, so a short defaults line is read as the question's own words (193: A36; 196: Fy 50 from the cover mixed with Fu 58 from the plates' A36). parseDefaults (491-502) understands neither a bare 'U = 1.0' nor 'A36 for plates', 'A992', 'Fu =' or 'N in bolts', so a long line silently drops the cover's U. The documented cover-U rule (1722) then never applies (197). pipeline.js coverLines (571) takes a one-line question that starts with 'unless noted' as cover AND keeps it as the question, so ctx holds it twice (145). findBolt (1214) returns the first diameter in the text, so an inline default '3/4 in bolts' beats the question's own '7/8 in bolts' (155).
clusters.fix_plan:
[named-steel-grade] reader.js + expand.js. No pipeline change. (1) FILL.lookup_material: collect the typed grades with markGrade's regex, extended to A53/A500 and 'Gr B/C'. Keep only distinct grades and the part's own text. Exactly one grade ON HER SLIDE (A36, A992, A572 [Gr 50], A53 [Gr B], A500 [Gr C]): B.set('what', canonical grade, m[0], 'high', 'the steel your question names'). ANSWER: look-07 36/58, look-08 36, look-09 50/65, look-10 Fu 58, g06 50/62, g07 36/58. A grade NOT on her slide (A500 Gr B, A572 Gr 42/55/60/65, A588, A242, A913, A529): B.ask(..., 'stop') with one sentence and no number ('Your question names a steel that is not on her steel slide; the page does not look it up. NOT answered here.'), so look-11 STOPs. Two different grades in one item: ASK which (need). A bare 'gr/grade NN' with no A-number, where NN differs from the product default Fy: STOP/ASK for the ASTM name (look-12). Never the A36 default. (2) expand.js parseMat: exactly two chunks, one holding only a shape/product and the next holding only a grade, separated by a comma (his ' ,A36'): return null, so the single reader takes it as ONE item (look-13/14 give 50/65 and 36/58). Keep the split for 'and'/'or' lists (g16). (3) FILL.lookup_critical_stress: after fillFy, if no Fy was read: (i) add GRADES rows A53 [Gr B] 35/60 and A500 [Gr C] 50/62 (reader table, not frozen data) and ANSWER look-16 (21.8). (ii) A typed A-grade that GRADES lacks (A500 Gr B) gives a STOP (look-18). (iii) With no grade, a product word gives her slide's steel (pipe 35, plate 36; HSS/angle/W stay 50) with confidence medium and a note 'her slide: <product> steel'. ANSWER look-15 21.8 and look-17 22.1, the same steel column_capacity already uses for a Pipe. (4) findGrade: record the distinct 'Fy = n' values of the part's own text. fillFy raises B.ask('fy_two', 'Two yield stresses are given. Which one is the member's?', ['Fy'], values, 'need') when there are two or more (look-19, x12). MUST NOT CHANGE: BL-023 family (A36 gusset plate), BL-025 family (A53 Gr B Pipe 6 STD), g15 'A36 plate', g16 list, 'Fy of a W14x90' (A992), 'gra de b' typing, typed 'Fy = 36 ksi' in calculation forms, and the f07 'phi Fcr ... A36' path. Run regress.sh: (4) touches every form, so classify each change.
[grade-and-cover-binding] Mostly reader.js. (1) findGrade: collect every grade match, in text order. Drop a grade with a negation or replacement before it (not|no|instead of|rather than|other than|except, ~20 chars). When the member is not a plate or bar, also drop a grade tied to a connection element: 'for plates', 'gusset', '(end|base|splice|connection) plates?', or 'plates? (are|is|of)' within ~25 characters. If one grade is left, use it (153: A572 gives 180; 174/145: A992 gives 359.2). If none is left, leave the grade null so the family default from her slide applies (W = A992), as today: 193 gives 502. If two different grades are left, ASK kind 'need' on Fy ('which steel is the member?'); never take the first. (2) splitPreamble: drop the length > 80 test for a line that starts with the cover marker and is not the last line; the 'last line is never preamble' rule stays. parseDefaults learns a bare \bU\s*=\s*(\d*\.?\d+), 'Fu = N ksi', 'A992' (rolled shapes), 'A36 for plates' (plates only) and 'N in bolts'. Each reader uses a default only when the question itself gives none. 196 and 197 then give 662.4 by the documented cover-U rule. (3) pipeline coverLines: a cover-marker line that is the only (or the last) line is the question, not cover, mirroring splitPreamble; a one-line hunk (145). (4) findBolt: gather every bolt diameter (kind 'bolt'). With two different sizes, the one outside a cover clause ('unless noted', 'assume', 'use ... unless') wins (155: 7/8 in gives 583.5); otherwise ASK kind 'need' on bolt_dia. MUST NOT CHANGE: a single grade anywhere in the text (the stem's grade reaching later parts through pickMatch); plate members 'PL ... A36'; 'A36 steel' columns where A36 really is the member; the loose 'Fy 36' and 'grade 50' forms; long cover lines typed in the defaults box (her Q23 'K = 1.0 for all columns', 'pinned support conditions', the loads-basis line); the 1722 cover-U exclusions.

clusters.title: A shape look-up answers the wrong property: a property typed WITH its value wins over the one asked, a ratio becomes one of its symbols (or two look-ups), 'nominal depth' becomes d, 'web and flange thickness' gives tf only, a single angle's minor axis becomes y, and '2 W14x90' prints the one-shape row
clusters.root_cause: [shape-property-pick] reader.js findProperty (l.780-805) loops over PROPS (l.774-779, order tw, tf, bf, Z, S, r, I, d, A, W) and takes the FIRST entry that matches ANYWHERE. (a) A given 'tw=0.44 in', '(Zx = 157)', 'bf = 6.49', 'tf=.38in', 'depth 14 in', '(its tw is 0.44 in)' beats the asked radius of gyration, section modulus, moment of inertia, flange width or area (look-29..34). (b) No ratio is read: 'rx/ry', 'Zx/Sx', 'h/tw', 'flange width to thickness ratio', 'ratio of rx to ry' give the first symbol or name (look-35, 37-40), and expand.js chunksOf (l.236) cuts at '/' into two look-ups (look-36, 41). (c) PROPS maps '(actual|nominal) depth' to d (look-42). (d) 'web and flange thickness' does not match /web\s+(?:width|thickness)/, so tf wins, and expand leaves 'web' as residue (look-59). (e) Weak/minor maps to y for every family (l.793-794). For a single angle the minor principal axis is z, and the engine HAS rz/Iz/Sz (checked: L4X4X1/2 rz 0.776, L6X4X1/2 Iz 3.54) (look-43..45). (f) A count of shapes is never read: findProperty needs 'of a/an/the' (l.783), so '2 W14x90' prints the full one-shape row. markBuiltUp (pipeline l.2793) covers only section_properties/column forms (look-60; also 'two C10x30 back to back' prints the C10X30 row).
clusters.fix_plan: [shape-property-pick] reader.js findProperty / FILL.lookup_shape + expand.js parseShape. (a) First, because it is the likely one (he types table values along): in the PROPS loop and in the sym rule, SKIP a match that is followed by a value (^\s*(?:=|:|is|of)?\s*\.?\d) and continue with the next entry. ANSWER: look-29 ry 3.70, 30 Sx 143, 31 Ix 204, 32 bf 6.49, 33 A 26.5, 34 Ix 999. If every property word is a given, keep today's behaviour. (b) Ratios: 'bf/2tf', 'flange (width-to-thickness|slenderness)' -> property 'bf/2tf'; 'h/tw', 'web (width-to-thickness|slenderness)' -> 'h/tw'. Both are rows of the frozen data and the engine answers them, so ANSWER 10.2 and 25.9. Any other ratio (two property symbols joined by '/', 'ratio of X to Y', 'X to Y ratio', 'shape factor') gives a STOP with no number ('a ratio of two properties is not looked up here'). expand.js parseShape returns null for the same texts, so it never splits a ratio (look-36/41). (c) 'nominal depth': STOP ('the nominal depth is the number in the shape's name; the page gives the actual depth d'). expand already declines it. (d) expand.js PW: add '(?:web\s+and\s+flange|flange\s+and\s+web)\s+thickness(?:es)?' -> two elements tw, tf, so it gives two look-ups, as 'tw and tf of' already does (ANSWER 0.345 and 0.575). (e) A single angle (kind L, not 2L) with weak|minor|z words: equal legs -> axis z (ANSWER rz 0.776 for look-43/44). Unequal legs -> ASK geometric y or principal z (look-45), because some books mean Iy. expand parseShape returns null for an L with a weak/minor axis word. (f) FILL.lookup_shape: a count (2-9, two..four, pair of, double, twin) right before a non-L shape name, a word count before an L name that findShapes did not read as 2L, or 'back to back' / 'side by side' / 'built-up' with one shape name gives a STOP with no number ('more than one shape: this look-up gives one rolled shape only'). MUST NOT CHANGE: 'Ix of W14x90', 'A of a WT12X88', 'tdes of HSS...', 'tw and tf of a w12x53' (two parts), 2L names, W/C weak axis = y, 'radius of gyration about the weak axis of a W14x90' = ry.
